text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Island's National Council discusses the killing of two Greek Cypriots on the Green Line dividing the island last month.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Australian MP condemns Turkish killings of protesters at Dherinia last month.
- Contractors are warned not to re-hire Turkish Cypriot workers.
- Political parties tried to put on a show of unity for at a conference of overseas Cypriots, but ended up squabbling on tactics.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Woolworth makes friendly takeover bid for the remaining 45 percent of Zako.
- Russian tourists spend $225 million on their package holidays to Cyprus.
- Russian Menatep bank inaugurates its Cyprus operations.
HARAVGHI
- The occupation regime in the north is looking for an excuse to provoke further incidents between the two sides.
- The Council of Ministers is to examine three different proposals for the privatisation of the motor vehicles inspection unit of the Communications and Works Ministry.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Political parties and the government yesterday agreed to use their respective influence to defuse tension in the free areas after the murders of Tasos Isaac and Solomos Solomos.
- Forty five percent of Zako is being purchased by Woolworth in a share swop.
- Mosques in the government-controlled areas will be the first target of Turks seeking to stir tensions.
SIMERINI
- Schools will start working this year with staff shortages.
- People place illegal bets worth 200,000 pounds each week on horse races.
- Women ask to join the army.
